The language the game runs in, chosen before you start. Saved in the game's config and used every launch until you pick another here (or in game, where it can also be changed and overrides this). Not every course or text string is translated, so a non-English language can still fall back to English in places.
The output resolution: the size of the final picture, the HUD included. The 3D scene can be drawn smaller than this and upscaled in the in-game menu (F10).

Ultrawide races: more of the track to the left and right, not a stretched picture. The HUD and the menus stay 16:9 in the middle. Needs a game built with this version (Setup, Build): an older build stays 16:9.

In game, F10 (or both stick buttons, L3 + R3, on a controller) opens a settings menu: upscaler, render scale, sharpening, frame generation, HDR, present mode, speed limit, an FPS counter and which controller plays as Players 1 to 4. The Enhancements tab holds the same settings.

Pins each of the game's main threads (and the renderer's) to its own CPU, so the caches stay warm instead of being refilled after every migration. It helps a little in heavy moments (fewer dropped frames). Leave it off if the CPU is busy with other programs, because pinned threads can't move away from them. Needs 6 or more CPU threads.

Preloads gperftools' tcmalloc: the renderer and the graphics hooks allocate a lot, and it is worth several fps in split-screen races. Install the gperftools package (libtcmalloc_minimal.so.4) to use it.
Logs the game's NVN graphics calls to user/log (nvn_trace.txt, nvn_frames.csv and two-frame captures every 30 s). Used to build the native GPU backend. Slower.

Packs the game built on this PC into one AppImage for this PC (never share it: it contains the translated game code). Saves, settings and mods move to ~/.local/share/kartrecomp and ~/.config/kartrecomp; your game files, firmware and mods are linked there, not copied.
Your game save (userdata.dat). Copy it to back it up.

Graphics quality: High uses the game's full effects, Low its lighter ones (the console's docked and handheld modes). The resolution is the same in both: it follows the output resolution and render scale. It can also be changed in game (F10). Changes are saved immediately and apply from the next launch; they are locked while the game runs.

Above 60, the renderer draws extra frames between the game's own (frame generation). The game's speed and physics do not change. It needs a temporal upscaler for the motion vectors: FSR 3 is switched on at 100% when no upscaler is chosen (Enhancements tab).
Rates above 60 need the FSR 3 or DLSS upscaler plugin (Enhancements tab).

Speed limit: 100 % is the game's normal speed; another value speeds up or slows down the whole game. In 3-4 player split-screen the game draws each view at 30 fps; "60 fps split-screen" on the Setup page builds a game that draws every view every frame.
